candidates.summary: the gate serves every namespace that holds a package as a person, so gno.land renders reserved namespaces as user profiles: "Gnome sys", "Gnome docs", "Gnome tests", "Gnome gov"
candidates.failure_scenario: GET /u/sys: buildContributions returns the r/sys/* realms, so len(contribs) != 0 and the userExists branch at 618 never runs. The page comes back 200 with Handlename "Gnome sys" (handler_http.go:652) and the system realms listed as that Gnome's contributions. Same for docs, tests, gov, archive, devrels, gnops. Of the 20 namespaces the examples tree deploys, 19 render "Gnome <name>" with no r/sys/users registration behind them; only std and stdlibs are excluded, and that is an accident of their paths failing weburl.Parse rather than a rule. A visitor reading /u/sys cannot tell a reserved namespace from a registered person, which is the distinction the PR title says the change draws.
candidates.verify_by: run tests/b1-lines-r2-user-gate-sweep.go at 876762bdf and read the gnomes-without-registration line; cross-check against the six RegisterUser calls in gno.land/genesis/genesis_txs.jsonl
candidates.evidence: RESULT gnomes-without-registration: aeddi archive demo devrels docs gnoland gnops gov jaekwon jefft0 jeronimoalbi leon mason moul nt onbloc samcrew sunspirit sys tests -- and RESULT genesisusers=6 lost=0 over gfanton123 zoo_ma123 moul001 piupiu123 anarcher123 ideamour123, none of which is in that list

candidates.summary: the accepting side of maxUsernameLen is pinned by nothing: the cap can be halved to 32 and the whole gnoweb package stays green
candidates.failure_scenario: The added test only feeds a 65-character name, which any cap below 65 rejects, so the constant is free to drift from the registry's own 64 (examples/gno.land/r/sys/users/errors.gno:19). Set maxUsernameLen to 32 and every registered name of 33 to 64 characters 404s at line 608 before any query runs, with go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ still reporting ok. The only thing holding the constant up at all is the incidental 9-character /u/zoo_ma123 route added to app_test.go, which pins it from below at 9.
candidates.verify_by: sed -i 's/^const maxUsernameLen = 64$/const maxUsernameLen = 32/' gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/handler_http.go && go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ -count=1
candidates.evidence: cap 32: 'ok  github.com/gnolang/gno/gno.land/pkg/gnoweb  7.200s'. cap 8: '--- FAIL: TestRoutes/test_route_/u/zoo_ma123', the only case that fires.

candidates.summary: the "renamed alias" subtest names a case userExists cannot distinguish: it and "unknown name" both end on (false bool) and take the identical branch
candidates.failure_scenario: userExists reads only the last line of the qeval body (handler_http.go:566-567). "unknown name" feeds "(nil *...UserData)\n(false bool)" and "renamed alias" feeds resolveNamePayload(false), whose last line is also "(false bool)". The struct line the alias fixture spends 2 lines building at 2008 is never looked at, so deleting resolveNamePayload and pointing "renamed alias" at the same literal as "unknown name" keeps both subtests green. A reader of the table believes the handler tells a renamed handle from a name nobody took; it does not, and no test would notice if that ever became true.
candidates.verify_by: point the "renamed alias" entry at the "unknown name" literal and run go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ -run TestHTTPHandler_GetUserView_NotAUser; expect green

candidates.summary: the two new integration routes are pinned to RegisterUser txs for real accounts in gno.land/genesis/genesis_txs.jsonl, and neither file points at the other
candidates.failure_scenario: TestRoutes gets its chain from integration.LoadDefaultGenesisTXsFile (app_test.go:47), which loads gno.land/genesis/genesis_txs.jsonl. That file carries exactly six RegisterUser calls; moul001 and zoo_ma123 are two of them, and each name appears in the whole tree exactly twice, once there and once here. Neither has a package, so both routes pass only through the new qeval branch. Edit or drop either registration in the genesis file and the gnoweb package goes red on a route table that says nothing about where the name comes from.
candidates.evidence: six registrations: gfanton123 zoo_ma123 moul001 piupiu123 anarcher123 ideamour123. grep -rln 'moul001|zoo_ma123' returns only gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/app_test.go and gno.land/genesis/genesis_txs.jsonl.

dropped.summary: the reserved @std and @stdlibs namespaces bypass the gate: vm/qpaths maps them onto the stdlib key space, so buildContributions comes back non-empty for a name nobody registered
dropped.settled_by: go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/ -run TestUserGateSweep -v at 876762bdf prints 'RESULT reserved   /u/std=404 /u/stdlibs=404'. The stdlib paths keeper.go:1699 returns are not domain-prefixed, so every one fails weburl.Parse at handler_http.go:520 and contribs ends empty; the name then falls to ResolveName, which says no.

dropped.summary: vm/qeval never yields ErrClientPackageNotFound, so the 'no user registry on this chain' arm is dead and a chain without r/sys/users 500s on every /u/ page
dropped.settled_by: gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm/keeper.go:1880 in withQueryEvalMachine returns ErrInvalidPkgPath("package not found: %s") when GetPackage is nil; errors.go:88 wraps InvalidPkgPathError{}, which gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/client.go:371-377 maps to ErrClientPackageNotFound. The arm is reachable.

dropped.summary: gno.Re_name is stricter than the r/sys/users rule, so a legitimately registered name 404s at the shape gate
dropped.settled_by: examples/gno.land/r/sys/users/store.gno:27 is reName = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z][a-z0-9]*([_-][a-z0-9]+)*$`), byte-identical to gnovm/pkg/gnolang/mempackage.go:70 Re_name once regx.Compile anchors it with ^ and $ (tm2/pkg/regx/regx.go:13-22). No name in the gap.

dropped.summary: vm/qpaths rejects names its own reUserNamespace does not match, so a name passing gnoweb's gate can make buildContributions error into a 500 instead of a 404
dropped.settled_by: gno.land/pkg/sdk/vm/keeper.go:1665 reUserNamespace = `^[~_a-zA-Z0-9/-]+$`, a strict superset of Re_name; every name the gate admits passes it.

dropped.summary: username[:4] and username[len-4:] slice without a length guard, so a short string accepted by crypto.AddressFromBech32 panics the handler
dropped.settled_by: tm2/pkg/crypto/bech32.go:19 AddressFromBech32 routes through AddressFromBytes, which requires exactly 20 bytes; a bech32 encoding of 20 bytes with hrp "g" is always 40 characters, so the slice bounds cannot be reached.
